newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks storm to record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German stocks storm to record closing high.

text.p: German stocks stormed to a new record high in Friday floor trading but pared gains in afterhours trading, falling victim to Wall Street's sharp drop at the opening.

While the blue-chip 30-share DAX index ended floor trade at a record closing high of 3,604.55, the first time the index has closed above the psychologically important 3,600 level, it fell in after hours trading.
The IBIS DAX index ened up only 0.12 percent or 4.41 points at 3,569.26.
Early in the session the market was underpinned by Wall Street's strong performance and a higher dollar as well as speculation of further consolidation in Germany's banking sector.
But with Wall Street dropping over 40 points in early trading, German gains began crumbling as well.
Traders also said the market may have simply lost steam, exhausted after days of trading at high levels. German markets are closed on Monday.

At the center of speculation about consolidation in the financial sector was talk that Bankgesellschaft Berlin, fresh from announcing talks of a possible merger with NordLB, might be considering taking on BHF Bank as well. Both sides however said there was nothing to the talk.
BHF finished floor trade up 3.40 marks at 46.30 marks.
